function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

message.content:
A **cronut** (pronounced “kron‑yoo”) is a hybrid pastry invented by French pastry chef Dominique Ansel in 2012. It combines elements of both croissants and donuts:

| Feature | Croissant | Donut |
|---------|-----------|-------|
| Shape   | Crescent / flaky layers | Ring-shaped doughnut |
| Texture | Light, airy laminated dough | Dense, sweet dough |
| Flavor | Butter-rich, slightly savory | Sweet glaze or filling |

Ansel’s original recipe uses a laminated dough similar to croissant dough but shaped into donut rings and then fried instead of baked. After frying, they’re glazed or filled just like traditional donuts.

The novelty—flaky butter layers inside a sugary ring—sparked an instant craze worldwide. Today you’ll find cronuts at specialty bakeries, pop‑up shops, and even some mainstream chains. They come in many flavors—from classic vanilla glaze to more adventurous options like matcha, salted caramel, or chocolate ganache.
